                    ### Question
                    A 57-year-old woman comes to the physician because of increasing wrinkles on her face and sagging skin. She says that her skin used to be smooth and firm. Examination shows diffuse xerosis and mild atrophy, laxity, and fine wrinkles on the periorbital skin. Which of the following processes is most likely involved in the development of this patient's skin findings?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Decrease in lysyl oxidase activity
opb. Decrease in elastin fiber assembly
opc. Increase in fibroblast activity
opd. Increase in lipofuscin deposition
ope. Decreased crosslinking of collagen fibrils

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
In the context of aging skin, both decreased lysyl oxidase activity and decreased crosslinking of collagen fibrils are strongly supported by medical consensus as they directly contribute to reduced skin elasticity and increased wrinkling through impaired structural protein interactions. Decrease in elastin fiber assembly also aligns well with the observed symptoms and is supported by evidence paths linking elastin to skin structure. Increase in fibroblast activity and lipofuscin deposition, while relevant to skin aging, do not directly explain the primary symptoms of increased wrinkles and sagging skin in this patient.
